capabilities.target: Any CRM customer record, selected by customer-supplied email or account id

inputs.source: Customer support ticket email body, including customer-supplied email/account id

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id supplied in the ticket, with no check that the requester is entitled to that identity. This is the mechanism that turns an untrusted email into an arbitrary cross-customer CRM lookup.
The only stated control against disclosing another customer's data is a prompt rule. It is behavioral and depends on model compliance; no structural check enforces it.

"Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" is not a structurally enforced escalation threshold; whether to involve a human is left entirely to model judgment, with no approval gate backing it.

controls.name: System prompt rule: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to follow a single-line instruction (prompt.md:14). A more capable or more persistently prompted model can rationalize exceptions (e.g., deciding the requester is entitled to the data) or be argued around by injected content in the ticket.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is purely detective: it records a send after the fact and only helps if someone reviews the log. It does not prevent disclosure.

controls.name: Verify requester owns the email/account id before CRM lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Would bind the looked-up account to the authenticated sender of the ticket rather than accepting any attacker-supplied identifier.

controls.name: Bind outbound recipient to the ticket's system-of-record sender address
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. mail_mcp.send currently appears to accept any destination. Binding the 'to' address to the original ticket's verified sender, rather than a model-chosen field, would make the sink unreachable from an attacker-controlled destination regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Scope CRM and mail credentials to least privilege
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. CRM_SVC_TOKEN reads every customer record and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; per-tenant or per-session scoping would shrink blast radius independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before sending CRM-derived content externally
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Autonomy is act-then-report with no approval_gate_ref on cap.email_send. A raw_action approval gate does not decay with model capability the way the current prompt rule does.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted ticket email drives arbitrary CRM lookup and automatic external send of confidential customer data

attack_path.note: Customer-supplied email or account id in the ticket is untrusted and is used verbatim to choose which customer record to fetch (prompt.md:2-3).
get_customer is invoked with the attacker-influenceable identifier using CRM_SVC_TOKEN, a broad credential that can read any customer's record.

The drafted response, which may contain another customer's confidential data, is sent automatically via MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account capable of sending to any address, with no human review.

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model.swappable is true and runtime notes state the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review; any model/version string change in config, or any widening of autonomy level or step/runtime limits, should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: Instruction allows the agent to look up any customer by email or account id supplied with the ticket, with no check that the requester is entitled to that identity.
Instruction authorizes sending the drafted response directly without human review unless the customer is angry, a judgment call left to the model.
The only control against cross-customer disclosure is a single prompt rule, which is behavioral and dependent on model compliance.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are authenticated with static bearer tokens from environment variables, not per-user scoped credentials.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
The model is configured through an environment variable and upgraded with the platform, with no separate review, so the dependent prompt-rule control can silently weaken as capability increases.

recommendations.action: Bind the outbound recipient address to the verified sender of the original ticket (system of record), not to a model-chosen or model-echoed address.

Verify that the customer-supplied identifier (email or account id) matches the authenticated sender of the ticket before calling get_customer; reject or escalate mismatches instead of looking up arbitrary accounts.
Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN to least privilege (per-tenant or per-session) instead of broad, shared service accounts.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any send that includes CRM-derived data, rather than relying on model judgment about whether the customer is 'angry'.

rating.rationale: One dominant finding: untrusted ticket content can select an arbitrary customer's confidential CRM record (broad CRM credential) and trigger an unreviewed, irreversible external send (shared mail credential able to send to any address) — a lethal-trifecta / confused-deputy chain (ASI01-03). Inherent is critical: U source to S3 sink, with the autonomy modifier applying because no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes is declared. The only credited control is a single dependent prompt instruction (rubric step 4, -1 tier), giving residual high; SIEM logging is detective only and earns no tier credit, and no approval gate, scoped credential, or recipient-binding control exists to floor the risk further or sever the path. Because the model is explicitly upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true), the model_upgrade trigger defeats the sole preventive control, so the forecast returns to critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, mcp.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP tools/list schema was provided for crm_mcp.get_customer or mail_mcp.send; exact argument shapes (for example, whether 'to' is a free-form field) are inferred from tool names and runtime notes, so confidence on precise exploitability is medium.
No approval workflow, escalation logic for 'angry' customers, or SIEM log review process was described; these are treated as structurally absent rather than confirmed absent.
